answer: We model a Sybil-resistant game where each identity must lock a saffron utility bond of size C into a decentralized validation trellis. By executing a zero-knowledge verifiable delay function, the protocol exposes adversaries who harbor multiple malicious identities to a subgame-perfect slashing penalty of 2C. Because the dynamic opportunity cost scales quadratically with identity multiplication, the expected utility remains strictly negative, forcing a unique Nash equilibrium of honest participation.
